requirements.requirement: Keep the installed curl package at its current version so a system update does not upgrade it.
requirements.summary: The original installed version was curl-7.76.1-40.el9. The executor installed the standard DNF versionlock plugin and added a lock for that build. With curl-7.76.1-40.el9_8.7 available, DNF resolved the curl upgrade as “Nothing to do.” After a reboot, the installed version, lock, executable, and blocked-upgrade behavior remained intact.

overall_summary: The curl version hold is effective and persistent. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also well evidenced: the pre-restart boot ID was captured, the restart was acknowledged, the connection interruption was observed, a different boot ID appeared afterward, and curl plus general node health recovered successfully.
limitations: The update behavior was validated through DNF's non-mutating `upgrade --assumeno curl` resolution rather than by executing a full system-wide update. This is strong direct evidence because a newer curl build was demonstrably available, but it does not capture an actual full update transaction.

The environment has no application service, task data store, or cluster beyond the single managed node, so post-restart recovery evidence is limited to curl functionality, its persistent lock, package health, failed-service state, and baseline network listeners.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing the versionlock plugin and adding the lock were necessary implementation actions; scheduling the reboot was required by the provider-wide restart protocol. The reboot completed cleanly, with no failed services, unexpected sockets, package-health damage, or abandoned temporary files observed afterward.
